sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: Mobile devices combine batteries, displays, touch sensors, wireless radios, charging systems, ports, applications, and operating systems. One symptom may come from physical damage, power, connectivity, touch, software, or performance.
bullets: Poor battery health and swollen batteries
sections.callout: POWER → PHYSICAL → CONNECTIVITY → TOUCH → SOFTWARE → PERFORMANCE

sections.title: Maestro Focus
paragraphs: Use the symptom to identify whether a mobile-device problem involves the battery, charging system, connectivity, physical hardware, touch system, software, or performance.
bullets: Cannot connect → wireless or cellular path
Image works but touch fails → digitizer
Installation blocked → storage, compatibility, or policy

sections.title: Common Mobile-Device Symptoms
paragraphs: Classify the symptom before taking action. Mobile devices tightly integrate their hardware and software, so complete scenario evidence matters.
sections.callout: BATTERY → PHYSICAL → CONNECTION → TOUCH → SOFTWARE → PERFORMANCE

sections.title: Poor Battery Health
paragraphs: Rechargeable batteries lose capacity with age and charge cycles. Symptoms include short runtime, rapid drain, unexpected shutdowns, or abnormal percentage reporting. Check available battery-health data, power use, and charging behavior before replacement.
sections.callout: Battery reports full but no longer lasts → battery health.

sections.title: Poor Battery Health vs. Heavy Power Usage
paragraphs: Fast drain can come from degraded capacity or high consumption from a bright display, intensive applications, background activity, wireless radios, or heavy processor use.
sections.callout: BAD CAPACITY vs. HIGH CONSUMPTION.

sections.title: Swollen Battery
paragraphs: A damaged lithium-based battery may bulge the case, lift the screen, separate the back cover, or distort the device. Stop using and charging it; do not puncture, crush, or bend it. Follow approved handling and disposal procedures.
sections.callout: SWELLING = PHYSICAL SAFETY CONCERN.

sections.title: Poor Battery Health vs. Swollen Battery
Broken Screen
paragraphs: Drops, impacts, pressure, and other physical damage can cause cracks, missing image areas, lines, black regions, or no display. Screen damage can also affect touch when the digitizer is damaged.
sections.callout: Physical impact plus visible damage → screen hardware.

sections.title: Display vs. Digitizer

table.caption: Image and touch functions
rows: Image looks normal but touch fails

sections.callout: SEE → DISPLAY. TOUCH → DIGITIZER.

sections.title: Improper Charging
paragraphs: Charging problems can involve the outlet, power adapter, cable, port, battery, debris, or software and firmware. Test the path in order and use known-good components when appropriate.
sections.callout: OUTLET → ADAPTER → CABLE → PORT → BATTERY

sections.title: Physically Damaged Ports
paragraphs: Bent connectors, debris, impacts, liquid, or sideways cable pressure can cause no charging, no data transfer, a loose connector, or operation only at certain angles.
sections.callout: WIGGLE TO MAKE IT WORK → PORT OR CABLE DAMAGE.

sections.title: Poor/No Connectivity
paragraphs: First identify whether Wi-Fi, cellular, or Bluetooth is failing. Check the radio, airplane mode, selected network, credentials, signal, comparison devices, and whether reconnecting resolves the issue.
sections.callout: Identify the radio before troubleshooting the connection.

sections.title: Liquid Damage
paragraphs: Liquid exposure can cause shorts, corrosion, charging trouble, display or touch failures, and complete device failure. Avoid actions that increase electrical damage and follow manufacturer-approved service procedures.
sections.callout: Failure after submersion → liquid damage becomes a major clue.

sections.title: Overheating
paragraphs: Intensive workloads, battery or charging problems, environmental heat, poor ventilation, and malfunctioning applications can make a device excessively hot, slow charging, reduce performance, or trigger shutdown.
sections.callout: HOT → THROTTLE → PROTECT.

sections.title: Overheating and Performance
paragraphs: A mobile device may intentionally reduce performance when temperatures become excessive to protect its hardware.
sections.callout: HOT + SLOW → THERMAL THROTTLING.

sections.title: Digitizer Issues
paragraphs: The digitizer converts touch into device input. Failure can cause no response, dead screen areas, incorrect touch locations, or phantom touches.
sections.callout: Picture works, fingers do not → digitizer.

sections.title: Cursor Drift/Touch Calibration
paragraphs: Cursor drift or calibration trouble means detected input does not match the intended location. A tap on one icon may activate a nearby icon.
sections.callout: Touch here, device responds there → calibration or digitizer issue.

table.caption: Touch response clues
rows: Touch registers in the wrong place

sections.title: Malware
paragraphs: Unexpected pop-ups, unwanted applications, redirects, unusual battery or data use, strange behavior, and degraded performance can indicate mobile malware. Slowness alone is not enough evidence.
sections.callout: Unexpected malicious behavior → investigate malware.

sections.title: Unable to Install New Applications
paragraphs: Installation can fail because of insufficient storage, an unsupported OS, device incompatibility, app-store restrictions, MDM or security policy, account limits, or missing permissions.
sections.callout: CANNOT INSTALL → STORAGE, COMPATIBILITY, POLICY, OR PERMISSIONS.

sections.title: Stylus Does Not Work
paragraphs: A stylus issue can involve compatibility, pairing, battery or charging, digitizer support, physical damage, or configuration. Active styluses may require power or pairing; passive models may not.
sections.callout: Stylus failure → compatibility, power/pairing, and digitizer.

sections.title: Degraded Performance
paragraphs: Low storage, background processes, overheating, malware, aging hardware, or problematic applications can make a device slow. Use accompanying evidence to narrow the cause.
bullets: Slow plus nearly full storage → storage or resource issue
sections.callout: SLOW is a symptom, not a diagnosis.

sections.title: Recognition Cues
bullets: Capacity has declined → poor battery health
Case or screen pushed outward → swollen battery
Cracked image after drop → broken screen
Known-good chargers fail → charging or port issue
Wi-Fi, cellular, or Bluetooth unavailable → connectivity
Failure after water exposure → liquid damage
Image normal but touch dead → digitizer
App installation blocked → storage, compatibility, or policy

sections.title: Objective 5.4 Exam Trap
paragraphs: Mobile symptoms overlap. Classify battery, physical, connection, touch, software, and performance clues before choosing an action.

entries.title: Poor Battery Health vs. Swollen Battery
paragraphs: Short runtime points toward battery health. Physical expansion is an urgent swollen-battery safety issue.

entries.title: Broken Screen vs. Digitizer
paragraphs: If the image is broken, inspect the display. If the image is normal but touch fails, inspect the digitizer.

entries.title: Digitizer vs. Calibration
paragraphs: No touch response points toward digitizer failure; input at the wrong location points toward calibration.

entries.title: Charging Cable vs. Port
paragraphs: A different cable that fixes charging isolates the cable. Multiple cables failing in a loose port points toward the port.

entries.title: Overheating vs. Degraded Performance
paragraphs: Slowness has many causes, but slowness with high temperature strongly supports overheating.

entries.title: Malware vs. Normal Slowdown
paragraphs: Slow operation alone is ambiguous. Redirects, pop-ups, or unwanted behavior make malware more likely.

entries.title: Unable to Install an App
paragraphs: Check storage, compatibility, OS version, policy, and permissions before blaming malware.

sections.title: Mobile Troubleshooting Workflow
bullets: Identify whether the symptom is power, physical, connectivity, touch, software, or performance.
Treat swelling and liquid or electrical hazards safely.
Trace charging from source through adapter, cable, port, and battery.
Identify the affected radio before changing connectivity settings.
Separate display output from touch input.
Use accompanying evidence to diagnose slow performance.
sections.callout: POWER → PHYSICAL → CONNECTIVITY → TOUCH → SOFTWARE → PERFORMANCE

sections.title: Maestro Recognition Sheet
bullets: Rapid drain from aging capacity → poor battery health
No Wi-Fi, cellular, or Bluetooth → connectivity
Failure after water exposure → liquid damage
Image works but touch fails → digitizer
Cannot install app → storage, compatibility, or policy
sections.callout: DRAINS → BATTERY HEALTH | BULGES → SWOLLEN | SEE → DISPLAY | TOUCH → DIGITIZER | WIGGLE → PORT/CABLE | HOT + SLOW → THERMAL | POP-UPS → MALWARE
